entities.summary:
Allianz Trade (formerly Euler Hermes), headquartered in Paris and owned by Allianz SE since 2018, is the world's largest trade credit insurance company — insuring approximately €995 billion in business transactions annually, covering 23,000 buyers in 160 countries, and providing the financial infrastructure that enables global trade by protecting companies against non-payment risk. Trade credit insurance — covering the risk that a buyer will not pay for delivered goods — is the invisible financial guarantee underlying approximately 10-15% of global trade flows.

Trade credit insurance emerged in the 1920s as international trade expanded and companies needed protection against foreign buyer default. The Hermes export credit guarantee agency (founded 1917 in Germany) merged with Credit Alliance (France) and Trade Indemnity (UK) to form Euler Hermes — covering three of Europe's major export economies. The 2018 rebranding to Allianz Trade connected the business to Allianz's 130-million-customer financial services network.

Allianz Trade's economic intelligence function — employing 400+ economists who monitor 80 million companies globally for financial distress signals — makes it one of the world's most sophisticated early-warning systems for corporate and sovereign credit risk. Its annual Insolvency Outlook reports are closely followed by governments, banks, and corporations planning trade and investment strategies. The COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2022) saw Allianz Trade insuring unprecedented volumes of trade receivables as payment defaults surged globally, demonstrating trade credit insurance's counter-cyclical stabilization function.
